literal: That which was digested having known, holding fast (to this rule), things that are not disagreeable let one eat, thoroughly having become hungry.
translation: Ascertaining that the previous meal is fully digested, and holding fast to this rule, eat only compatible foods after becoming thoroughly hungry.
modern: முன்பு உண்ட உணவு செரித்ததை அறிந்து, அதனை உறுதியாகக் கடைப்பிடித்து, உடலுக்கு மாறுபாடு இல்லாத உணவுகளை நன்கு பசித்த பிறகு உண்ண வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the fundamental rules of eating for maintaining good health. First, one must ensure that the previously consumed food is completely digested ('அற்றது அறிந்து'). Second, one must wait until a clear, strong hunger is felt ('துவரப் பசித்து'). Third, one must eat only those foods that are compatible with one's body and do not conflict with each other ('மாறு அல்ல'). Adhering firmly to these guidelines ('கடைப்பிடித்து') prevents disease and eliminates the need for medicine.
